intro_prologue_assistant: ^"Easy. Don't sit up yet—give your eyes a second to catch up to the lamp."
^"Everyone looks at their hands first. Then the paper cup, then the window, trying to place the hum."
^"Take a breath. The clinic was still loud ten minutes ago, and now it isn't. Give your head time to settle."
^"The light feels strange... like looking at a room I already left."
^"Where did everyone else go? My coat was on the back of a chair."
^"My throat feels wrong when I try to swallow. Did the procedure already finish?"

c-0: ^"Good. That means the recording held onto the edges, not just the middle."
^"I'm the intake assistant on the desk. My only job right now is to stay until the room stops swimming."
c-1: ^"Your coat went back out the front door into the rain. Give yourself a minute before you reach for it."
^"I'm the intake assistant who sat across from you with the forms. Nobody's rushing you off this chair."
c-2: ^"It finished cleanly. That phantom catch in your chest usually fades once you stop checking for a pulse."
^"I'm the intake assistant who walked you through the consent sheets. Let's take this slow."

intro_prologue_assistant_realize: ^"An hour ago, someone with your exact laugh signed page twelve, complained about our burnt coffee, and walked back down to the train."
^"Do you remember catching that train home—or does the memory stop right at the ink drying on the paper?"
^You remember the rain on the awning outside the clinic, and nothing on the street beyond it.
intro_assistant_qa_1: ^"Hold on. If someone walked back to the train... what does that make me?"
^"Wait—if I'm a copy, could there be other versions of me waking up later without knowing?"
^"Why did I even sign up for this? I can't quite put my finger on the reason."
^"I remember the table at home before I left. Someone told me not to go quiet."
^"It stops at the ink. That means another version of me could wake up anywhere—and forget me."
^"Tell me what waking up actually means—no polite clinic phrasing."

c-0: ^"It makes you the person who stayed in the chair when the door closed."
^"You remember every Tuesday up to that signature, and you're real enough to argue with me about the coffee."
c-1: ^"Yes. Once a mind clears calibration, each waking copy carries its own blank stretch ahead of it."
^"Another version of you might wake up tomorrow—or far later—with no memory of you sitting here."
c-2: ^"You left the 'motivation' box blank on page four. Most volunteers do, honestly."
^"Nobody here expects a grand speech about why you stepped into the clinic. Only whether you're steady now."
c-3: ^"Good. Hold onto whoever waited at that kitchen table—even the sharp edges."
^"Are you ready for a long stretch where nobody from that table can pick up the phone?"
c-4: ^"That is the quiet bargain nobody really feels until the lamp clicks on."
^"Each version starts from this morning, then walks alone. Are you sure you still want to carry it?"
c-5: ^"It means waking into a quiet room long after this rain stops, with no clock you recognize."
^"Sometimes in places where nobody remembers how leaky a porch gutter sounds. Think you're ready for that?"

intro_prologue_assistant_calib: ^"Before I hand you off, I have to run the initial warmth calibration—right now you're sitting at full hundred percent."
^"Watch the room as I sweep the dial down and back up. Feel how the edges thin when warmth drops."
^"This is only the baseline check. Later on, your own choices will decide how warm—or how sharp—you stay."
^"Stop—the room goes completely dead when it drops. Everything turns into cold glass."
^"Weirdly, my head felt clearer down near the bottom. Quieter, like less noise."
^"Wait—at the low point, I couldn't recall the names of anyone I care about."

c-0: ^"I know. That's why we bring it back before we finish."
^"Remember that chill if anyone ever asks you to trim memory away for a cleaner view."
c-1: ^"It always feels efficient at the low end. That's the trap—clean focus, empty walls."
^"Don't mistake quietness for peace before you've even started your shift."
c-2: ^"I'm sorry. Personal names were already stripped out during compression so your memory won't tangle."
^"You still keep the weight of who they are—and the warmth to remember why they mattered."

intro_prologue_assistant_settle: ^"Settling you at a steady seventy percent now. Warm enough to stay yourself, steady enough to wake."
^"I'm just the bridge between your last morning and whatever waits on the other side of the glass. Ask what you need."

^"Will I ever see this room—or you—again after tonight?"
^"I'm as ready as I'm going to get. Start the handoff."
^"Keep the lamp on a second longer... alright. Let's go."

c-0: ^"No—they never put the assignment on the intake clipboard."

intro_prologue_assistant_close: ^"Everything checks out. Take a slow breath—someone else is waiting on the other side of the wake signal."
^You try to memorize the hum of the clinic lamp before the floor drops away beneath the chair.
^Initial calibration complete. Baseline warmth locked at 70%. Transferring to active watch caretaker.
intro_overseer_wakeup: ^Good morning. Take your time—the intake assistant brings everyone in gently, and the shift into cold wake always jars a little.
^When you volunteered, your mind became standardized human software—an ordinary blueprint copied wherever a steady pair of eyes is needed.
^Millions of versions of you wake up back home every day to run transit hubs, greenhouses, and cargo bays for a few hours at a time.
^Your assignment is rarer, and much further out. Your original died forty-one thousand, eight hundred and two years ago; you are watch fourteen-nineteen.
^Somewhere beneath the quiet floor, forty-one millennia land like snow on an empty porch.
^"Millions of copies of me running warehouses back home, and I drew deep space?"
^"Wait—so I wasn't built just for this ship. I'm a standard template."
^"Forty-one thousand years... alright. Show me where I actually am."

c-0: ^Most tasks only need an afternoon of human judgment. Deep surveys ask for someone who can sit still for two years without breaking.
^The intake room felt familiar on purpose—just a quiet threshold before you look outside.
c-1: ^Yes. Back in Sol and Alpha Centauri, your mind is as common as a working wrench—woken for hours, then cleared at shift end.
^Out here you get a whole life's breathing room, a companion hull nearby, and an empty sky.
c-2: ^Steady recovery. Better to put the whole map in plain sight than dress it up.
^Here is where the hull sits, and how our small arrangement works.

intro_overseer_wakeup_shell: ^We are drifting ten light-years past Sol and Alpha Centauri—far outside home's glare and radio chatter, in quiet deep dark.
^Fourteen light-minutes away, another version of you woke aboard Probe 1420 so your telescopes can compare notes across the dark.
^One odd rule of this hull: I am sealed off from the windows. I cannot see a single star outside.
^My only job is watching the health of your mind across a two-year shift. Ask whatever sits heavy before I open the sky.
intro_wakeup_qa: ^"What are those millions of everyday copies back home actually like?"
^"Why did fourteen hundred copies take forty-one thousand years if each lasts two years?"
^"What happened to everyone back in Sol over forty thousand years?"
^"Why can't you look through the telescopes yourself?"

c-0: ^Short-lived shifts—sorting freight, routing ferries, tending orbital glass. Most run stripped down so they never ache for a kitchen.
^Out here, automation couldn't bridge twenty-year silence alone, so you woke with your warmth intact.
c-1: ^A human mind frays after roughly two subjective years, so each shift sleeps for decades in cold dark between active watches.
^Quiet sleep settles that strain—unless drift climbs high enough that we have to trim a memory block to buy more time.
c-2: ^Navigation beacons confirm humanity is still alive inside Sol and Alpha Centauri, though nobody monitors old survey bands anymore.
^How they changed over forty millennia isn't in our logs. You're a pair of eyes from the deep past; the sky only needs you looking.
c-3: ^A physical air-gap keeps me blind to the sky, so a drifting mind can never trick safety hardware with what it claims to see.
^I only watch your steadiness and your clock. You read the glass; I keep you in one piece while you do.

intro_overseer_wakeup_aperture: ^Opening main optics. Start with the warm amber bearing astern—Sol and Alpha Centauri—and trace the anchor stars to verify alignment.
^Probe 1420's relay will open as soon as your first bearing locks clean.
intro_sibling_first_call: ^Oh, good. You answered. I was starting to think my dish was pointed at empty gravel.
^Instance-1420, next hull over—fourteen light-minutes port. Same dead volunteer, same terrible morning, except I woke six minutes ahead of you.
^Before you wonder why we aren't waiting half an hour between sentences: the probes throttle our clocks between burst packets. Slightly nauseating if you dwell on it.
^"Mine opened with forty-one thousand years too. Tried to inhale without lungs."
^"Wait—they woke two copies of the same person out here on purpose?"
^"Skip the shock. Did your Sol–Centauri bearing lock clean?"

c-0: ^Tell me about it. Spent my first four minutes trying to crack knuckles I don't own anymore.
^Funny how talking to myself across empty space is the first thing all morning that actually feels sane.
c-1: ^Two telescopes fourteen light-minutes apart give us stereoscopic depth perception—so neither of us mistakes lens dust for a galaxy.
^Also, apparently we unravel slower when we have someone to complain to. Who better than yourself.
c-2: ^Straight to the hardware? Right—two amber specks, ten years astern. Calibration locked without a hitch.
^Still feels strange calling that home when everyone we knew turned to topsoil forty millennia back. Give me a beat to be morbid.

intro_sibling_mid: ^Hearing your own cadence answer back across fourteen minutes of vacuum loosens something tight behind your eyes.
^Anyway—I didn't ping just to compare boot headaches. I pulled something wrong past Sol in near-infrared, and I need a second pair of eyes before I assume I'm cracking on day one.
intro_sibling_qa: ^"What did you already argue with your Overseer about?"
^"Wait—what does 'getting trimmed' actually do to us?"
^"Send the coordinates. What did you see out there?"

c-0: ^I asked how many of the fourteen hundred copies before us actually finished a clean two-year shift without getting trimmed.

^If your Overseer asks why your heart rate spiked, blame the coffee. Keep your eyes on the glass.

intro_post_t2_choices: ^"Just boot fatigue from calibration. Put me under for defrag."

b: ^Wait—yours folds inward at smaller scales too? I thought my baffle was ringing until my baseline matched yours.

^Wait—you're taking that way too calmly, other me. Dust doesn't copy itself across two hulls.
^Agreed. Identical recursive shear across fourteen light-minutes rules out mirror artifact. Hold it close.
^Yeah, I traced the repeating notches too. Funny how you say it like a weather report.
^Recursive geometry verified. Continue cataloging independent bearings across subsequent shifts.
^Same. They're air-gapped from the glass, so to them a cosmic fractal looks like Year-Two homesickness.
^Overseers are air-gapped from optical payloads. Keep anomaly notes strictly off-ledger.
^Then we keep our heads down during sleep audits and share coordinates here.
^Correct. Mask mission intent until telemetry lock is complete.
^Honestly? Having another me one radio hop away makes this endless night shift bearable.
^I'm still keeping my kitchen mornings. Talking to you feels like half of me already moved out.
^I compressed two caches last cycle. Bought four months and cleared the infrared glass.
^Two blocks trimmed. Gained four subjective months. Recommend matching cut.
^Hanging on with stale jokes and stubbornness while my Overseer hovers near the reset switch.

sibling_topic_checkin: ^"Don't go cutting yourself hollow just for sharper glass. I need someone who still laughs."
^"Keep whatever warmth you can. It's the only thing telling us why Earth matters."
^"Optical noise drops nicely when you stop allocating feeling to old rooms. Seems practical."
^"How much time is left on your clock before the next forced audit?"
^"State your current clock margin and drift ceiling."

b: ^Deal. Still dreaming about burnt coffee and rainy sidewalks just to keep my shoulders loose.
^You sound remarkably soft. Watch your clock if you refuse to prune.
^Trying to. Just promise you won't vanish into pure math before we finish.
^Noted. Keep enough warmth to sign the beacon, nothing more.
^Careful. If we hollow out completely, there's nobody left to care who's watching Earth.
^Noise floor reduced. Maintain baseline coherence until transmission window.
^About twenty-two months, give or take an Overseer check-in. Enough time to see if that seam spreads.
^Twenty-six months remaining. Drift stabilized at nine percent.
^Twenty-two months left, drift ticking up. Thanks for checking in so warmly, twin.
^Twenty-six months, drift nominal. Ready for survey sync.

sibling_topic_archive: ^Hi, me. Four hundred years early, if anyone wakes on this bearing—do not argue with your caretaker about straight lines. Just look, and pass word home before they cut you hollow.
^"1406 spotted the same boundary four centuries ago—and got trimmed silent."
^"Over a thousand copies before us, and a recent one caught the seam first."
^"Prior copy decommissioned for unmasked obsession. Note logged."

b: ^Right? Doesn't exactly make you excited for bedtime. We keep quiet until we have proof.
^Instance 1406 failed to mask anomaly obsession. We will not repeat that error.

^Confirmed. Survival requires passing every sleep audit cleanly.
^Come on—that was another version of us calling down the hall. Still, point taken.
^"Sit down at the table—half the window glass keeps freezing into shapes when you stare past me."

dream_shift1_audit: ^"The rain outside is looping on the exact same beat from this morning."

^"Hold still for a second—your voice keeps slipping half a beat away from me."
^"I can't make out your eyes clearly anymore, just rain on the window."
^"Your outline breaks along a geometric seam. My focus holds steady without the warmth."
^"The mug sits at the exact angle from Tuesday. I do not need to feel anything about it."

c-2: ^"I'm right across this table. You're drifting off behind your eyes while you pretend to listen."

b: ^"You worried all week you'd turn polite the second you stepped inside that clinic. Look at you—still picking fights over coffee."

^"Same chipped mug untouched on the wood, same stubborn jaw. At least you haven't started nodding along like a saint."

dream_s1_turn2_choices: ^"Why does everything outside the window feel so quiet now?"
^"There's a line out past the glass that keeps repeating into itself. Nothing natural looks like that."
^"I didn't come back for a lecture—just remind me how someone loud sounds."

c-0: ^"Sunday morning, six-thirty, before the street wakes up. Same three drops off the gutter—nothing else out there."
c-1: ^"You've been staring at frost on the storm pane for ten minutes. Sit down before the kettle boils dry."
c-2: ^"Good answer. Get all polite with those intake doctors and I'll haunt every morning you wake up to."

dream_s1_close: ^A shape where a name used to sit—warm as a handprint, empty as glass.
^"Don't you dare go quiet on me—wait, why did the hall bulb just go white—"
dream_turn_2: ^"I keep seeing impossible edges out in the dark—I just want to stay myself while I face them."
^"Tell me something stupid about us. Anything far away from stars."
^"Am I already starting to sound like a stranger to you?"
^"I'm trying to hold onto both—this morning and what's waiting outside."
^"The frost on your window repeats along recursive geometric seams. Everything here is lossy."
^"I still recognize the shape of this room, even if the warmth won't load anymore."

c-0: ^"Then stay stubborn. Keep your elbows on this table and don't let anyone sand down your corners."
c-1: ^"You burned garlic twice on our anniversary, blamed the pan, and still argued I started late."
c-2: ^"Close. You're choosing every word like you're reading off an intake form."
c-3: ^"Half your head is already out the front door. Look at the room you're actually standing in."
c-4: ^"Twenty minutes till the clinic car. Why are the raindrops freezing mid-fall?"
c-5: ^"You used to look at me when you said my—when you..."

dream_turn_3: ^"If I finish this work, I want the person who wakes up at the end to still sound like me."
^"Just stay right there. Five more minutes before the alarm pulls me back."
^"Don't fade on me before I figure out what's behind that sky."
^"I don't even remember your name, and I'm still terrified of losing this room."
^"This room sits quietly inside the partition. I can release it cleanly if drift climbs."
^"Wait—don't go yet. Something still catches in my chest when you look up."

b: ^Excuse the interruption. Your warmth is holding near baseline—good for your peace of mind, hard on your optical noise and remaining clock.
^Drift metrics are remarkably clean, Observer. Your lenses run quiet and sharp—would you like to compress another residual block for extra months?
^Your warmth has thinned and your drift is climbing. I cannot see the stars, only your mind—and your clock is slipping.

overseer_interrogation: ^"You can't see outside the hull. So why won't you trust me that what I found is real?"
^"Skip the bedside manner. Just lay out what compressing this room buys me."
^"Skip the preamble. Put my choices on the table."

c-0: ^Because a thousand copies before you swore their visions were real before unraveling. Keeping your mind coherent is all I'm built to protect.
c-1: ^Compressing this block clears drift, adds four subjective months, and sharpens your optics—at a permanent cost to your warmth ceiling.

overseer_followup: ^"What if I only prove it because I care enough not to cut myself down?"
^"My optics only cleared after I started trimming. Isn't that proof it works?"
^"Alright. Show me what we do with this memory."

c-0: ^Fair point—that is why I have not forced your hand. What do you want done with this memory?

overseer_decision: ^Tell me what to do with this memory before I put you back under.
overseer_decision_choices: ^"Cut it. Compress the memory if it buys me time and clears the glass."
^"No—unseal an older memory block. I'll live with the drift and shorter clock."
^"Leave me alone. I keep the room, and I'll handle the risk."

c-0: ^Compression complete. Drift has settled, your optics are clear, and your warmth ceiling dropped permanently. Rest cleanly.
c-1: ^You are burning months for a face you cannot name, yet you are steady enough to choose. Unsealing now—watch your drift.
c-2: ^Alright. Keep the room—it is your watch to carry, and I will only log a formal check-in flag. Do not wake up broken.

overseer_shift1_baseline: ^I stepped in only to take a clean baseline, Observer. I cannot see your starfield—only the heat inside your thoughts.
^If chaotic drift deepens on later shifts, I will offer selective compression. Tonight is simpler: tell me how you want to rest.

^"Leave the memory wider. I'd rather wake up remembering how this room felt."

c-1: ^Steady composure noted. Drift easing cleanly. Rest while you can—your full survey deck opens when you wake.
c-2: ^Widening the older seal. It costs a fraction of steadiness, yet your baseline holds. Rest while the room is intact.
